name: nteli-quoting
description: Turn an RFQ, RFP, spec or email into a priced, standards-checked quote, then an order, for manufactured equipment: UL 508A control panels, switchgear, data center pods, HVAC, pump skids, hazardous-location enclosures, medical gas, cable assemblies and more.

interface.longDescription:
Nteli Quoting takes a customer's RFQ, RFP, spec sheet or email to a priced, standards-checked quote, and on to the order, for engineered, configure-to-order equipment. Estimators, application engineers, inside sales teams, manufacturer's reps and dealers at specialty manufacturers use it for quotes, estimates, bids and proposals, without rebuilding a spreadsheet for every job. It works for configure-to-order and engineer-to-order products.

Product lines:
- Industrial control panels (UL 508A)
- Power packages: switchgear, transfer switches, UPS, generators and battery storage
- Distribution transformers
- Data center pods and modular data centers: white space, power train and cooling
- Commercial HVAC, cooling towers and boilers
- Packaged pump skids and water treatment systems
- Hazardous-location and explosion-proof enclosures and panels (Class I, Division 1 and 2)
- Instrumentation and controls
- Medical gas outlets, manifolds and headwalls
- Lab casework and fume hoods
- Electronic assemblies, cable assemblies and wire harnesses
- Fire doors and door hardware
- Commercial kitchen ventilation hoods
- Cranes and hoists
- Accessibility lifts: platform lifts, stair lifts and vehicle lifts
- Surgical robotic systems
- NRE for engineering and design services

Paste the request into ChatGPT. The engine works out which configurations are valid and asks only the questions that change the answer, one at a time, each with the price it leads to. Panels and data center pods are built from their parts: list the drives, starters and I/O, or the racks and kW per rack, and the engine sizes the enclosure, breakers, UPS, generators, busway and cooling. When requirements clash, it says which rule is in the way and offers the ways out. Jobs outside the standard range go to a Specials team instead of getting a guessed price. Values the customer didn't state are marked as assumptions and listed to confirm.

The quote lists every part, what to confirm and the standards it was checked against (NEC, NFPA, UL, NEMA, ASHRAE), with good / better / best options side by side. Panels come with a preliminary submittal sheet. It all happens in an interactive card: tap an answer, assume a default, switch options, undo, submit for approval.

Every price and compatibility answer comes from Nteli's rules engine, not the model. Sign in with a work email: the first person at a company creates its workspace and picks its product line.
defaultPrompt: Quote a 480 V control panel for 3 pumps on VFDs, 25 hp each, with a PLC and an HMI on the door.
Quote a 1 MW data hall pod: 40 racks at 25 kW, N+1, rear-door cooling, 480 V.
Quote an outdoor panel in a Class I Div 1, Group D area with controls inside and a viewing window.

positive.description: A data center pod sized from racks and kW
positive.prompt: Quote a 1 MW data hall pod: 40 racks at 25 kW, N+1, rear-door cooling, 480 V.
positive.expected_behavior: A data center assembly with rack PDUs, busway, UPS, generators, switchgear and cooling sized by the engine, a price, and the unstated site facts (fault current, utility) held as questions. With 40 racks in one row (20 at most) it is marked not yet quotable and the rows can be split.

positive.description: A control panel built from its devices
positive.prompt: Quote a 480 V control panel for 3 pumps on VFDs, 25 hp each, with a PLC and an HMI on the door.
positive.expected_behavior: A control panel assembly with three drive groups; the enclosure, main breaker, PLC and cooling are sized by the engine and shown in the card with a price.

positive.prompt: Quote an outdoor panel in a Class I Div 1, Group D area with controls inside and a viewing window.
positive.expected_behavior: The question card: the next question that changes the price, each answer with its price, and an Assume option; nothing is saved.

positive.description: A priced pump skid with options
positive.prompt: Quote a duplex process pump skid for a hydrocarbon, about 500 gpm, medium head, Class I Div 2, outdoors, 460 V.
positive.expected_behavior: A priced skid with Good / Better / Best options, its main parts and the standards it was checked against.

positive.description: A combination that isn't allowed, and the ways out
positive.prompt: Quote a Class II Div 1 panel for a Group D gas area.
positive.expected_behavior: The conflict card: Class II is for combustible dusts and Group D is a gas, so the engine offers the ways out as priced taps (a Class I Div 1 gas area, or a Class II dust group) instead of a price.

negative.description: A code question with no quote asked for
negative.prompt: What does NEC 430.52 say about motor branch-circuit protection?
Write a cover email to send my customer with the quote attached.
What's the weather in Houston tomorrow?
